name: Skeuomorphism
visualIdentity: Supplemental reference: controls resemble functional physical objects through materials, lighting, edges, and shadows. Presses and rotations should visibly match state changes; labels stay readable. Not claimed as a named style in the source collection.
suitableUses: Explicitly suited to interface concepts where physical resemblance aids use, including audio plugins, hardware companion apps, tutorials, and premium hardware simulators. It can also support product demonstrations and explanatory sequences. These are source-backed examples; other uses are inferred.
limitations: Avoid decorative textures without function, low-contrast engraved labels, and mismatched lighting. Preserve supplied product colors and materials. Use exploded reveals only for separable parts whose relationships they explain; camera orbit requires real 3D or clearly labeled parallax. Omit audio-card tilt when it obscures content or the voice metaphor confuses the topic.
palette: No intrinsic palette is specified. Optional fallback tokens for new presentation elements only: background #E7DFD0, foreground #3A352D, accent #8B7151. Exact task, brand, reference, semantic, and asset colors take precedence; preserve roles and families, add no hues or gradients. Accent with background text fails the 4.5 body-text target; verify actual composites.
motionAndInteraction: Use legible, state-linked presses and rotations. Compatible patterns include bounded pointer tilt with neutral return, reversible chapter handoffs, finite horizontal card tracks with snap selection, story steps, meaningful component reveals, and bounded camera orbits when supported. Interactive HTML may use pointer, scroll, swipe, buttons, keyboard, focus/touch equivalents, and reduced-motion states. Video must author these states on deterministic composition time, with reading holds and direct/backward seek support; no live input dependency.
audio: No fixed soundtrack is specified. Suggest music, narration, vocals, effects, ambience, or silence for the subject and audience; respect supplied choices. Audio playback, waveform, and spatial panning are optional and independent of visual tilt. Use actual authorized audio, synchronize with picture, and check speech clarity, balance, clipping, and alignment.
assetRequirements: Construct knobs, scales, buttons, and feedback from the chosen object model using HTML/CSS and SVG where suitable. Prerender complex materials when appropriate; keep labels as readable text. Preserve source imagery and product materials. Prepare/cache stateful assets; do not imply simulated physics is validated. Real orbit needs 3D assets; exploded views need meaningful separable parts. Voice or waveform UI needs actual audio/data.
combinations: Works alone when physical resemblance aids use. Product motion can clarify control states; prerendered metal or leather plates can add fidelity if lighting matches and labels remain text. Compatible narrative, carousel, or reveal patterns are optional and should serve content. Avoid conflicting progress drivers, unreadable depth, unrelated effects, or transitions that obscure causality.
productionApproach: Select visual construction and motion tools by fidelity and action; HTML/CSS and SVG are core, GSAP is the primary seekable motion layer, with Motion optional only when synchronized. HyperFrames handles composition, timing, media/audio sync, validation, and export; Remotion only if unavailable or a verified limitation blocks a requirement, with reason recorded. Keep rendering and motion separate from export; inspect frames and full output.
